cost: one full build cycle + a .NET decompile
what: pac solution pack failed for both package types: all 15 OptionSet files were wrapped in a redundant outer <optionsets> element, and Role/Workflow/FieldSecurityProfile/EntityRelationship files stored identifying values as child elements where the packer expects root-element attributes.
expected: hand-authored file shapes inferred from documentation would pack
root_cause: the SolutionPackager file-layout contract was inferred, not ground-truthed. Resolved only by decompiling SolutionPackagerLib.dll with ilspycmd.
why_it_was_never_caught: no gate compared hand-authored component files against a shape the platform itself produced
lesson: Never infer a SolutionPackager file shape from documentation. Create the smallest real instance, export + unpack it, and copy the shape exactly.

proposed_change.summary: ground truth before authoring; two failed guesses is the signal to stop guessing

cost: two revisions of false PASS on a HARD constraint
what: `gitleaks detect` ran without --no-git, so it scanned commit HISTORY instead of the working tree. For two revisions none of the 47 files under src/solutions/ was tracked in git, so C-TECH-001 recorded PASS while covering none of the delivered source.
expected: the secret scan covered the files the build packages
root_cause: gitleaks' default scan target is git history, not the working tree; the flag that changes it was absent
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing asserted the gate's scan SCOPE; a gate reporting PASS over zero relevant files is indistinguishable from a clean one
lesson: `gitleaks detect` scans commit HISTORY by default. Without --no-git it can report PASS over none of the files the build actually packages.

proposed_change.summary: assert --no-git present in config and prove the gate fails on a planted private key

cost: one BLOCKED build, resolved by relocating a file
what: secret-scan BLOCKED build #5 on a real provisioning certificate (REV-Provisioning-SP.pfx/.cer) sitting in provisioning/certs/ — untracked and already gitignored, so no version-control leak existed.
expected: a gitignored, never-committed file would not fail a secret gate
root_cause: the gate scans the whole working tree by design (correctly, per IMP-0002) but has no allowance for deliberately-local credential material
why_it_was_never_caught: first build in which a certificate was present on disk during a scan
lesson: Credential material (.pfx/.cer/.pem) must live OUTSIDE the repo, not merely gitignored — secret-scan reads the working tree, correctly, and will block the build.

proposed_change.summary: credential material lives outside the repo, not merely gitignored

cost: undetected across builds #1-#4
what: build.yml's `lint` step ran BEFORE `pack-managed` and pointed --path at the unpacked source folder. `pac solution check` requires a packed .zip and fails immediately with "the value passed to '--path' is invalid".
expected: the lint step had been executing and passing since it was written
root_cause: two defects at once: wrong step order (consuming an artefact a later step produces) and wrong input type (folder where a .zip is required). Masked because `auth` and `lint` were deferred together in every prior build, so the step never executed to fail.
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing verified that a step's inputs exist or are produced earlier; and a DEFERRED step was reported as SUCCESS rather than as a coverage gap
lesson: `pac solution check --path` takes a PACKED .zip, never a source folder — and it must run AFTER the pack step that produces it.

proposed_change.summary: preflight input availability, step order, and tool input-type contracts

cost: 3 test fixes mid-build
what: Three hardcoded schema-count assertions went stale (16->17 option sets, 88->94 rev_application attributes, 34->38 secured columns), broken by the agent's own approved schema additions in the same session.
expected: tests would not break from approved in-scope work
root_cause: tests assert absolute counts rather than deriving them from source, so any legitimate schema addition breaks them
why_it_was_never_caught: inherent to count-coupled assertions; they fail on every change, correct or not
lesson: A test asserting an absolute schema count breaks on every legitimate schema addition. Expect to fix counts when you add columns; do not assume the test found a defect.

proposed_change.summary: candidate: derive counts from source, or assert invariants rather than totals. Deferred - needs a reviewed decision, not a silent edit

cost: a whole DEV deployment shipped with 0 forms and 0 views
what: pac solution pack silently dropped every file under each entity's FormXml/ and SavedQueries/ folders - 0 warnings, 0 errors - because Entity.xml declared no <FormXml /> / <SavedQueries /> marker element. The solution shipped to DEV with 8 view files and 4 form files on disk and none created.
expected: files present in the source tree reach the target environment
root_cause: the packer requires an empty marker element to make a folder reachable; without it the folder packs to nothing, silently
why_it_was_never_caught: root-components-resolve does not cover SavedQueries/FormXml (they are not RootComponent-declared types), and neither pac solution pack nor pac solution check warns
lesson: An entity's FormXml/ and SavedQueries/ folders are dropped SILENTLY at pack time unless Entity.xml declares the empty <FormXml /> / <SavedQueries /> markers. 0 warnings, 0 errors, 0 components created.

proposed_change.summary: assert every FormXml/SavedQueries folder with content has its marker element

cost: unknown - undetected since the line was authored
what: The `no-special-category-data-in-scoring` step - a HARD FR-016 / DUAA 2025 compliance gate - targeted the scoring flow's path WITHOUT its .json extension. It never read the flow, from the day it was written.
expected: the gate greps the scoring flow for special-category column references
root_cause: `grep -r` on a nonexistent literal path exits 2 (error, not 'no match'), and the step's leading `!` inverts any non-zero exit into a pass. Every grep failure mode became a PASS.
why_it_was_never_caught: no gate verified that a gate's own target path exists; and no negative test proved this gate could fail
lesson: The `! grep ... && echo` gate pattern turns EVERY grep failure — including 'target does not exist' (exit 2) — into a PASS. Verify the target path exists before trusting any such gate.

proposed_change.summary: dead-target check + mandatory negative test for every inverted-grep gate

cost: caught pre-deploy, one edit
what: rev_careprovidedexample's shipped Entity.xml <Description> still named rev_carersupport, a column removed in the same build.
expected: removing a column removes references to it
root_cause: prose inside shipped metadata is not covered by any reference-integrity check
why_it_was_never_caught: found only by unpacking the packed zip and grepping for the removed column names - an ad-hoc check, not a gate
lesson: Prose inside shipped metadata (a <Description>) can name a column you removed. Unpack the packed zip and grep for removed names before declaring the build clean.

proposed_change.summary: candidate gate: no shipped Description may name a column absent from the solution

cost: 4 of 11 seed rows failed live, after 7 had already written
what: rev_setting.rev_description is MaxLength=500. Four seed-settings rows written in this project's verbose documentation style exceeded it and failed with a Dataverse validation error, mid-run.
expected: settings rows would seed cleanly
root_cause: a platform field-length limit that nothing in the build read - deploymentSettings/*.json was not covered by any gate
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing in the build parsed the deployment settings files at all
lesson: rev_setting.rev_description is MaxLength=500. This project's verbose documentation style exceeds it. Same class as the flow 256-char cap.

proposed_change.summary: assert every settingRows[].description within the column's declared MaxLength

cost: a lost artefact download, not investigated
what: pac solution check reported its results downloaded to solution-checker/, but the directory was empty afterwards. Attributed to the repo path containing spaces; not investigated further because the PASS result was captured from stdout.
expected: the checker writes its report where told
root_cause: unconfirmed - suspected space-in-path handling in the CLI
why_it_was_never_caught: the build reads the result from stdout, so the missing file changes nothing that is asserted
lesson: This repo's path contains spaces. `pac solution check --outputDirectory` silently writes nothing; read the result from stdout instead.

proposed_change.summary: record that this repo's path contains spaces and which tools mishandle it

cost: manifests for builds #1-#3 permanently lost; #6 overwrote #5
what: artifact_output was hardcoded to build/artifacts/revitalise-grant-automation-20260810-1/ and reused for every build from 08-10 to 08-17. Six builds wrote into one directory, against WORKFLOW.md's mandated <slug>-<date>-<n>/ convention.
expected: each build has its own artifact directory and retained manifest
root_cause: a date-stamped literal path in config, with nothing asserting it matched the convention or changed per build
why_it_was_never_caught: no gate compared artifact_output against the WORKFLOW.md convention; the manifest is not read back by anything, so its loss was invisible
lesson: Each build gets its own artifact directory via scripts/resolve-artifact-dir.py. Never hardcode an artifact path: six builds once shared one directory and three manifests were lost.

proposed_change.summary: resolve <slug>-<date>-<n> per build; every step references $ARTIFACT_DIR

cost: latent - no real Entity.xml was affected
what: verify-forms-and-views-reachable's has_marker() regexed the RAW file text, so an <FormXml /> appearing inside an XML COMMENT satisfied the gate and a genuinely missing marker would go unreported.
expected: only a real marker element satisfies the check
root_cause: regex over raw text without stripping comments first
why_it_was_never_caught: found only while building the known-bad fixture for this gate - the fixture's own explanatory comment named the elements in tag form and the gate passed
lesson: A structural check that regexes raw XML text can be satisfied by a marker inside a COMMENT. Strip comments before asserting on element presence.

proposed_change.summary: strip XML comments before the marker check; regression test added

cost: 15 pac solution import attempts / ~2 days
what: Fifteen import attempts to get the solution into DEV. Six root causes: FieldSecurityProfile element shape, fabricated Role GUIDs, three successive wrong guesses at AppModuleSiteMap.xml, AppModule.xml almost entirely wrong, connection-reference component type 10371 unrecognised as a RootComponent, and an environmentvariabledefinitions folder layout taken from an older pac version.
expected: hand-authored solution source would import
root_cause: every failure was a plausible guess about a platform contract, committed to source, and validated only by gates that could not detect it being wrong
why_it_was_never_caught: pac solution pack validates layout, the 640-test Pester suite validated internal consistency, the XML gates validated well-formedness - all three passed, none could see the defect
lesson: Every one of fifteen import failures was a plausible guess about a platform contract, committed to source, validated only by gates that could not detect it being wrong. Two failed guesses is the signal to stop guessing and go get ground truth.

proposed_change.summary: C-TECH-050/051/052 + skills/how-to-verify-a-platform-contract.md

cost: 3 of the 15 attempts
what: Three failures imported cleanly, were queryable via the Web API, and still left a flow no maker could open or save: 62 description fields over the 256-char cap, a stray runtimeConfiguration.staticResult block, and a concurrency/operationOptions conflict.
expected: a successful import means the component works
root_cause: import acceptance (V3) and designer usability (V4) are different properties; nothing tested the second
why_it_was_never_caught: no automated check can open a flow in the designer - V4 requires a named human step, which did not exist as a gate
lesson: A successful import proves the component was ACCEPTED, not that it works. Three components imported cleanly, were queryable, and still could not be opened or saved by a maker.

proposed_change.summary: C-TECH-053: report only the verification level executed; V4 is a named step with a named owner

cost: a second deployment session
what: After a 'successful' import: no views on any table, no forms on any table, and rev_setting had zero rows.
expected: a successful import created what the source declared
root_cause: see IMP-0006 for forms/views. Settings rows are data, not solution components, and were never seeded.
why_it_was_never_caught: the deployment's verification step queried environmentvariabledefinitions, appmodules, sitemaps and workflows - savedquery and systemform were absent from that list
lesson: After an import, query EVERY declared component type by name. A hand-written subset of types to check will omit the one that failed — savedquery and systemform were both absent from the list that 'verified' the first DEV deploy.

proposed_change.summary: query EVERY declared component type by name after import, from a list derived from source, not a hand-written subset

cost: one reviewer-found defect + a re-deploy
what: A-001's guessed multi-select control classid was wrong: the dropdown rendered with no options on three fields. The Unvalidated Assumptions Register had recorded it as OPEN, severity E2, 'pending V4' - and it shipped anyway.
expected: an assumption the register flags as unvalidated does not reach an environment unclosed
root_cause: C-TECH-052 requires RECORDING a guess; nothing requires CLOSING it before deploy. The register predicted this failure precisely and was wired to nothing.
why_it_was_never_caught: the register is advisory. test-agent's fail conditions do cover an OPEN assumption, but the deploy proceeded regardless.
lesson: An Unvalidated Assumptions Register row that is still OPEN is a prediction of a live defect, not paperwork. Close it before deploying, or expect the reviewer to find it.

proposed_change.summary: Stage 0.5 blocks while any §10 assumption is OPEN and closeable in the target environment

cost: one reviewer-found defect + a re-deploy
what: The 11 scored-answer fields (rev_feelingscaleanswer, rev_wellbeinganswer1-10) carried generic form labels ('Wellbeing Answer 1') instead of the real survey questions. Pre-existing, not introduced by that pass.
expected: form labels show the real questions
root_cause: the correct wording existed in each attribute's own Entity.xml description but was never copied onto the form label
why_it_was_never_caught: no test asserts form label TEXT - only structure. Verbatim from the incident record: 'never caught because no test asserts form label text'.
lesson: No test asserts form label TEXT. Labels can be structurally perfect and semantically wrong; check them against the attribute's own authored wording.

proposed_change.summary: candidate gate: form control labels must match the attribute's own displayname/description where one is authored

cost: a multi-step transitional-import sequence
what: Dataverse rejects a Picklist->String/Boolean type change via solution import ('Attribute rev_helperrelationship is a Picklist, but a String type was specified'). The subsequent delete attempt returned 400 because a FORM DEPENDENCY blocked it - the column had to be removed from the form via a transitional import first, then deleted, then recreated at the correct type.
expected: a column type change ships like any other schema change
root_cause: two undocumented platform procedures discovered by execution: type changes are not importable, and deletes are blocked by form references
why_it_was_never_caught: no document described the procedure; it had never been attempted
lesson: Dataverse rejects a Picklist->String/Boolean change via solution import, and the follow-up delete is blocked by any form that references the column. Procedure: strip the control from the form in a transitional import, delete, then recreate at the correct type via the Web API.

proposed_change.summary: record the column-type-change procedure: strip from form, delete, recreate via Web API

cost: caught only by an independent query
what: rev_hearaboutus and rev_otherhearaboutus were silently NOT created by an import that reported success. Caught only because ensure-schema.ps1 afterwards reported them CREATED rather than EXISTS.
expected: a successful import created every declared component
root_cause: solution import can report success having skipped components
why_it_was_never_caught: second instance of IMP-0013's class, two days later. Nothing was added after the first to query every declared component by name.
lesson: Solution import can report SUCCESS having silently skipped components. This is the second recorded instance; treat 'import succeeded' as a claim to verify, never a result.

proposed_change.summary: same as IMP-0013 - this is the second instance, so it must generalise, not be patched again

cost: STILL OPEN as of 2026-08-17
what: Solution import RELABELS matching option values but does NOT delete values the new source omits. rev_breaktype retains 4 stale values (6-9), rev_applicanttype retains 1 (value 4). Correct new values are present and correctly labelled; these are extra orphans.
expected: the imported option set matches source exactly
root_cause: import semantics are additive/update-only for option values
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing compares live option-set members against source after import
lesson: Solution import RELABELS matching option values but does NOT delete values the new source omits. Orphaned values survive every subsequent import. Compare live option-set members against source.

proposed_change.summary: OPEN: cleanup needs DeleteOptionValue (declined by the session safety classifier, IMP-0021) or reviewer action in the maker portal

cost: one blocked cleanup, still outstanding
what: The DeleteOptionValue API call needed to clean up IMP-0019's orphaned values was declined by the session's own safety classifier.
expected: a scoped metadata cleanup call executes
root_cause: destructive-sounding metadata operations can be refused by the harness regardless of authorisation
why_it_was_never_caught: not a code defect - an operating constraint of the environment the agents run in
lesson: Destructive metadata calls (DeleteOptionValue) may be refused by the session's safety classifier regardless of authorisation. Route these to the reviewer via the maker portal.

proposed_change.summary: record which cleanup operations require reviewer action in the portal instead

cost: the reviewer had to re-teach a working procedure
what: The certificate-from-Mac-keychain procedure, worked out and used successfully on 08-16, was unavailable the next day. The reviewer restored it: 'yesterday you moved and got the certificate from the mac keychain. Make it so that you can use that again.'
expected: a capability established once stays available
root_cause: pipeline-agent loads only its pipeline.yml and one knowledge file. Nothing carries an established capability across sessions.
why_it_was_never_caught: there was no read-back path of any kind - no agent reads prior logs, manifests, or the handover document
lesson: The provisioning certificate is in this Mac's CurrentUser/My keychain (thumbprint A6F94E1801D1C62B7A82AE75E1AA5AD243ECC7FE, app id 077f1f90-3218-4a06-bc90-887464353aa7). Cert-based app-only auth to DEV works from there — do not ask the reviewer to re-supply it.

proposed_change.summary: read logs/known-failure-modes.md on activation; capabilities section carries established procedures

cost: 8 findings written where nothing can process them
what: Eight [FINDING] entries were improvised into logs/routing.log - a log whose documented format is one routing decision per line and which no agent reads back.
expected: a finding has somewhere to go
root_cause: agents needed a findings channel and none existed, so they used the nearest writable log
why_it_was_never_caught: nothing validates log line formats, and nothing reads routing.log at all
lesson: Findings belong in logs/improvement-log.jsonl. logs/routing.log is one routing decision per line and is read by nothing.

proposed_change.summary: this file. The 8 entries stay in routing.log as history; future findings come here.

cost: one failed build step, caught before commit
what: The known-bad fixture written for the secret-scan gate spelled a PEM private-key marker as a literal inside src/tests/build/BuildGates.Tests.ps1, so the repo's own secret-scan step matched it and failed the build.
expected: a negative test for the secret scanner would not itself be a finding for the secret scanner
root_cause: a credential-shaped literal committed to source to test a credential scanner is indistinguishable, to that scanner, from a real leak
why_it_was_never_caught: caught on the first full build run after the gate was written - which is the point: the gate self-test suite was itself only proven by executing the whole build, not by writing it
lesson: A negative-test fixture for a scanner must not be a literal in source. Assemble the pattern at runtime from fragments, or generate the fixture into a temp directory, so the fixture is real at execution time and invisible at rest.

proposed_change.summary: assemble the PEM marker from concatenated fragments at runtime

cost: would have failed every CI run; undetected since the step was written
what: The `unit-tests` step's command was not valid shell. Its `Install-Module` call sat on a MORE-INDENTED line inside a YAML `>` folded scalar, so the newlines were preserved and `&& pwsh ...` began its own line — bash rejects that with "syntax error near unexpected token `&&'".
expected: the step as configured runs in CI
root_cause: YAML folded scalars preserve newlines on more-indented lines. The value yq hands to `bash -euo pipefail -c` was therefore genuinely multi-line with a leading operator.
why_it_was_never_caught: every build to date ran interactively, with the agent invoking Pester directly; no build had ever executed this config through scripts/ci/run-config-steps.sh. Nothing shell-parsed the command strings.
lesson: In a YAML `>` folded scalar, keep every line at the SAME indentation and put `&&`/`||` at line END — a more-indented line keeps its newline and yields a shell syntax error. Preflight now runs `bash -n` on every step command.

proposed_change.summary: check_shell_syntax: bash -n every step command

cost: one failing test in the first real CI-path run
what: A Pester test name containing angle brackets ('returns the <slug>-<date>-<n> shape...') threw "The variable '$slug' cannot be retrieved" under the build's own runner (src/tests/Invoke-Tests.ps1), while passing under a plain `Invoke-Pester -Path` which silently substituted empty strings.
expected: a test name is inert text
root_cause: Pester resolves `<foo>` in a test name as a data-driven template placeholder against $foo. Two invocation paths disagreed about whether an unset placeholder is an error.
why_it_was_never_caught: the two test-invocation paths behave differently and only one is used in CI; nothing ran the suite through Invoke-Tests.ps1 until the build was executed end-to-end through its real path
lesson: Never put angle brackets in a Pester test name — `<foo>` is a template placeholder resolved against $foo. And verify the suite through `src/tests/Invoke-Tests.ps1`, the path CI actually uses, not only `Invoke-Pester -Path`.

proposed_change.summary: remove angle brackets from the test name; note the two-path difference
